_readme: Day 7 benchmark. dev = 24 answerable (Day-6 dev 18 + Day-6 test 6, re-labelled dev because Day-6 test was already viewed) + 3 absent; test = 6 NEW answerable (written from the corpus before any Day-7 run) + 2 absent. Filters are user-context (chapter being read), never derived from gold.

questions.question: What does the idea of garbage in, garbage out say about the quality of a system's results?
questions.expected_answer: The quality of the output is determined by the quality of the input.

gold.evidence: garbage in, garbage out (GIGO), which means that the quality of output is determined by the quality of the input

questions.question: In a DBMS, where is the information that describes tables and fields kept?
questions.expected_answer: In a catalog called the data dictionary.

gold.evidence: In a DBMS approach, metadata are stored in a catalog called a data dictionary.

questions.question: Who has the final say over who may access a dataset and how it may be used?
questions.expected_answer: The data owner.

gold.evidence: The data owner has the authority to ultimately decide on the access to, and usage of, the data.

questions.question: Which data management role runs regular data quality checks and investigates root causes of quality problems?
questions.expected_answer: The data steward.

gold.evidence: The data steward performs extensive and regular data quality checks, initiates corrective measures or deeper investigation into root causes of data quality issues

questions.question: What is the price of guaranteeing full isolation of concurrent transactions in a relational database?
questions.expected_answer: Significant additional processing time.

gold.evidence: guaranteeing full isolation in a RDBMS requires significant additional processing time.

questions.question: Why are relational systems a poor fit for data such as free-form documents?
questions.expected_answer: Their rigid row-based schema with type constraints makes them not good at storing unstructured or semistructured data.

gold.evidence: RDBMS are not good at storing unstructured or semistructured data.

questions.question: Who first proposed the relational model of data and in which year?
questions.expected_answer: Dr. Edgar F. Codd of IBM Research, in 1970.

gold.evidence: The model was first proposed by Dr. Edgar F. Codd of IBM Research in 1970.

questions.question: Which relational algebra operator is not directly implemented in SQL?
questions.expected_answer: The Division operator.

gold.evidence: Note that the Division operator is not directly implemented in SQL.

questions.question: What conditions must a table satisfy to be in third normal form?
questions.expected_answer: It must be in 2NF and have no transitive functional dependencies.

gold.evidence: Tables in 3NF must be in 2NF and have no transitive functional dependencies.

questions.question: What is the focus of online analytical processing?
questions.expected_answer: Using operational data for tactical or strategic decision-making.

gold.evidence: In online analytical processing (OLAP), the focus is on using operational data for tactical or strategical decision-making.

questions.question: How does the IEEE define software engineering?
questions.expected_answer: The application of a systematic, disciplined, quantifiable approach to development, operation and maintenance of software.

gold.evidence: defines software engineering as the application of a systematic, disciplined, quantifiable approach to the development, operation, and maintenance of software

questions.question: Which generic framework activities (phases) make up a software process framework?
questions.expected_answer: Inception, elaboration, construction and deployment.

gold.evidence: A process framework generally encompasses four framework (or generic) activities: inception, elaboration, construction, and deployment.
encompasses four framework (i.e., generic) activities that are also known as phases: inception, elaboration, construction, and deployment

questions.question: How does the cost of keeping software running over its lifetime compare with the cost of building it?
questions.expected_answer: Maintenance/continuous deployment cost often exceeds the cost of construction.

gold.evidence: the cost of software maintenance/continuous deployment today often exceeds the cost of software construction

questions.question: For which kind of application is responsiveness especially critical because prices must be displayed and orders processed in real time?
questions.expected_answer: A brokerage system, where performance is important.

gold.evidence: In a brokerage system, performance would be an important requirement because the software system will need to display prices and process users’ orders in real time.

questions.question: What is the main criticism of traditional prescriptive process models?
questions.expected_answer: They are too rigid and inflexible, unsuitable for rapidly changing requirements.

gold.evidence: Traditional models are generally criticized for being too rigid and inflexible.

questions.question: What is the role of an architect?
questions.expected_answer: Chapter 8 context: the information architect designs the conceptual data model (blueprints) bridging business processes and the IT environment.

gold.evidence: An information architect, also known as a data architect or information analyst, is responsible for designing the conceptual data model (blueprints) to bridge the gap between the business processes and the IT environment.

questions.question: What does a database administrator do?
questions.expected_answer: Chapter 9 context: focuses on data storage, organization and access associated with a software solution.

gold.evidence: database administrators, who focus on areas such as data storage, organization, and access associated with a software solution

questions.question: How is scalability defined?
questions.expected_answer: Chapter 9 context: the measurement of the work and cost to increase a system’s throughput.

gold.evidence: scalability, which is the measurement of the work and cost to increase a system’s throughput

questions.question: If one of the courses is full during a student's registration, what happens to the registration transaction?
questions.expected_answer: The transaction will not complete successfully (atomicity).

gold.evidence: If that is not possible because one of the courses is full, the transaction will not complete successfully.

questions.question: Which relational algebra operations form a complete set?
questions.expected_answer: Select, Project, Union, Rename, Difference and Cartesian product.

gold.evidence: The following set of relational algebra operations is a complete set: Select, Project, Union, Rename, Difference, and Cartesian product.

questions.question: For what kinds of projects are Agile process models generally not suitable?
questions.expected_answer: Large, high-risk or mission-critical projects.

gold.evidence: In general, Agile process models are not suitable for large, high-risk, or mission-critical projects.

questions.question: What is the role of an architect?
questions.expected_answer: Chapter 9 context: the enterprise or solution portfolio architect makes high-level design decisions on modeling/solution design building blocks and their interconnections.

gold.evidence: enterprise or solution portfolio architect, who makes high-level design decisions on high-level modeling or solution design building blocks and their interconnections

questions.question: What name is given to software that is built into hardware such as a smartwatch or a car control system?
questions.expected_answer: Embedded software.

gold.evidence: Software that is integrated with hardware and can include both application and system software features is called embedded software.

questions.question: What does a database administrator do?
questions.expected_answer: Chapter 8 context: responsible for implementation and monitoring of the database and ensuring it runs efficiently in collaboration with network and system managers.

gold.evidence: The database administrator (DBA) is responsible for the implementation and monitoring of the database as well as ensuring databases run efficiently

questions.question: What does the term miniworld (universe of discourse) refer to in a database context?
questions.expected_answer: A miniworld represents some aspect of the real-world data that are stored in a database.

gold.evidence: A miniworld, or universe of discourse (UoD), represents some aspect of the real-world data that are stored in a database

questions.question: Which DBMS component translates statements written in a high-level language into low-level instructions for the query evaluation engine?
questions.expected_answer: The data description language (DDL) compiler.

gold.evidence: The data description language (DDL) compiler translates statements in a high-level language into low-level instructions that the query evaluation engine understands

questions.question: Is it possible to be employed as a software engineer while knowing only a single programming language?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, it is possible but not common.

gold.evidence: It is possible, though not common, to be employed as a software engineer knowing only a single programming language

questions.question: In a UML class diagram of a domain model, what do the numbers at the associations express?
questions.expected_answer: They are multiplicities, e.g., exactly one Car per AdaptiveCruiseControl.

gold.evidence: The numbers at associations are multiplicities, and they say that there is exactly one Car associated with each AdaptiveCruiseControl

questions.question: What does logical design ignore when a solution is designed?
questions.expected_answer: Logical design ignores any physical aspects.

gold.evidence: Logical design ignores any physical aspects

questions.question: Which example is given for a Geographic Information Systems (GIS) database application?
questions.expected_answer: Google Maps.

gold.evidence: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) applications (e.g., Google Maps)
